title: Primary Storage: RAM, ROM and Cache
purpose: Preserve the former Code First plus original exam questions and answers before replacing the opt-in You Do preview with RHS 2022/2024 sourced bank questions. Live source file is not edited.

code_first.q: Predict which message appears if free RAM is 900 MB.
code_first.code:
freeMB = 900
neededMB = 700
if freeMB >= neededMB then
    print("Load")
else
    print("Wait")
endif
p: Change neededMB to 950 and predict again.
Change the comparison to > and test the equality case.
code_first.a: Load; after changing neededMB to 950 it prints Wait. With > and equal values, it prints Wait.

original_exam_questions:
State whether RAM is volatile and describe what happens to its contents when power is lost. [2]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
Volatile [1]; contents are lost when power is removed [1].

Explain why a CPU benefits from cache memory. [3]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
Frequently used data/instructions stored in cache [1]; CPU can access them faster than RAM [1], improving speed/reducing waits [1].

Compare RAM and ROM using purpose and volatility. [4]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
RAM stores currently running programs/data [1] and is volatile [1]; ROM typically stores firmware/startup instructions [1] and is non-volatile [1].

stretch.task: Modify the Code First program so that when there is insufficient RAM it also prints the shortage in MB. Test freeMB = 900 and neededMB = 950.
stretch.hint: Only subtract when neededMB > freeMB. The shortage is neededMB - freeMB.
stretch.answer: With freeMB=900 and neededMB=950, the program prints Wait and shortage 50 MB. Add inside else: print(neededMB - freeMB).

mastery.task: Adapt the code for two applications. Use appA = 400 MB, appB = 550 MB and freeMB = 900 MB; compare the combined requirement with free RAM. Test again when both applications total exactly 900 MB.
mastery.hint: Set neededMB = appA + appB, then use >= so the equality case is accepted.
mastery.answer: 400 + 550 = 950 MB, so the output is Wait with a 50 MB shortage. When total required is 900 MB the output is Load because freeMB >= neededMB. This models the decision; actual memory allocation has further overheads.
